intro: Each model uses the symbols of its own literature, so that a bound reads the same here as in the papers it comes from. Inside one model a symbol has exactly one meaning. The same letter may mean different things in different models (for example $n$ counts nodes on graphs and robots in the plane); essays that cross models say which model a symbol belongs to. Where a paper writes a different symbol for the same quantity, the table says so under *papers write*. Symbols that a single paper defines for its own result are defined where they are used and listed under that problem.

general.meaning: asymptotic notation, as $n$ (or the stated parameter) grows; $\tilde O$ hides polylogarithmic factors
an arbitrarily small positive real (a constant unless stated)
a positive constant whose value does not matter for the statement
time: a round, or a point of time in an asynchronous execution
in synchronous settings (FSYNC, SSYNC, synchronous agents), one step in which every activated entity performs one full cycle

in asynchronous settings, an interval of time in which every entity completes at least one full cycle; it need not be the shortest such interval. The execution is divided into consecutive epochs, and a bound of $X$ epochs holds for every such division. Programmable matter calls the same notion an *asynchronous round*
